title: Authenticity of the A10–A12 Compositions
summary: Privacy in the nE sense follows from ivE security for A10–A12, but proving authenticity from the A1–A9 assumptions or finding counterexamples remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the $\text{ivE} + \text{vecMAC}$ to $\text{nAE}$ compositions $A10$, $A11$, and $A12$, privacy in the $\text{nE}$ sense follows from security of the underlying $\text{ivE}$ encryption scheme, but it is unresolved whether they provide authenticity under the same $\text{ivE}$-security and PRF-security assumptions used for $A1$--$A9$. The open task is to determine whether those assumptions generically imply authenticity for $A10$, $A11$, and $A12$, or to construct counterexamples showing that they are insufficient. [S1]

scope.domain: Generic composition of ivE and vecMAC for nAE, specifically constructions A10, A11, and A12.
assumptions: ivE security of the underlying encryption scheme
PRF security as assumed for A1–A9
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the ivE-security and PRF-security assumptions used for A1–A9 generically imply authenticity for A10, A11, and A12, or whether counterexamples show those assumptions insufficient.

progress.summary: The source states that nE privacy follows from ivE security and that authenticity holds under an additional knowledge-of-tags assumption. Under the A1–A9 assumptions, it reports neither an authenticity proof nor a counterexample.
citation_labels: Chanathip Namprempre et al., Reconsidering Generic Composition
